s.t: “Behold”, from “הִנֵּה”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection.
When rendered in ALL CAPITAL LETTERS, “LORD” or “GOD” is the translation of God’s Proper Name (Hebrew “יהוה”, usually pronounced Yahweh).
or, suitable for, or appropriate for.
cherubim are powerful angelic creatures, messengers of God with wings. See Ezekiel 10.
The word translated “anew” here and in John 3:7 (ἄνωθεν) also means “again” and “from above”.
The same Greek word (πνεῦμα) means wind, breath, and spirit.
The phrase “only born” is from the Greek word “μονογενη”, which is sometimes translated “only begotten” or “one and only”.
The same word can be translated “disobeys” or “disbelieves” in this context.
“Raca” is an Aramaic insult, related to the word for “empty” and conveying the idea of empty-headedness.
literally, kodrantes. A kodrantes was a small copper coin worth about 2 lepta (widow’s mites)—not enough to buy very much of anything.
not in the Bible, but see Qumran Manual of Discipline Ix, 21-26
NU reads “acts of righteousness” instead of “charitable giving”
NU omits “For yours is the Kingdom, the power, and the glory forever. Amen.”
